finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If the input file path contains a shell metacharacter or an OS command
finding.assumptions: The file path provided as a command-line argument could be manipulated to execute a shell command

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that std::ifstream::open (line 78) merely opens a file whose name is given in argv[1]. The C++ standard library does not invoke a shell or execute the path as a command. No subsequent code uses the file path in a system(), popen(), or similar call. Therefore there is no OS command injection path from the command‑line argument.

finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
finding.trigger: If the input file contains unexpected data that could lead to an OS command injection
finding.assumptions: The word bank file could contain special characters that are not properly handled

parsed.refutation_attempt: The code never invokes any OS‑level command execution primitives such as system(), popen(), execve(), or similar APIs.  The only interaction with the file system is reading a file stream into a std::string and storing those strings in a vector.  There is no code that concatenates user data into a command string or passes it to a shell.  Therefore the reported OS command injection vulnerability cannot be triggered from the provided source data.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: If the input words contain a shell metacharacter or an OS command
finding.assumptions: The input words could be manipulated to execute a shell command

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the entire program for calls to system(), exec*, popen(), or any other function that could invoke an OS command. The only place the untrusted input words are used is within the recursive wordLadder function (lines 125‑161), where they are compared and passed to further recursive calls. No external command execution is performed.

finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
finding.trigger: If the input words contain unexpected data that could lead to an OS command injection
finding.assumptions: The input words could be manipulated to execute a shell command

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked for any OS command execution functions (e.g., system, exec, popen) or indirect command construction. No such calls exist in the code. The only operations involving the untrusted inputs are string comparisons, pushes onto a vector, and output via std::cout. Thus there is no path from the input words to an OS command execution.
